raw: CHAPTER VII. A Knock at the Door
en: [Chapter 7] A Knock at the Door

raw: “I have saved him.” It was not another of the dreams in which he had often come back; he was really here.
en: “I have saved him.” This was not another of the dreams in which he had so often returned; he was really here.
ko: “내가 그를 구했단다.” 이것은 그가 그토록 자주 돌아왔던 꿈 중 하나가 아니었다. 그는 정말로 여기에 있었다.

raw: And yet his wife trembled, and a vague but heavy fear was upon her.
en: Yet his wife shivered, filled with a quiet but heavy fear.
ko: 그러나 그의 아내는 조용하지만 무거운 두려움에 사로잡혀 몸을 떨었다.

raw: All the air round was so thick and dark, the people were so passionately revengeful and fitful, the innocent were so constantly put to death on vague suspicion and black malice, it was so impossible to forget that many as blameless as her husband and as dear to others as he was to her, every day shared the fate from which he had been clutched, that her heart could not be as lightened of its load as she felt it ought to be.
en: The atmosphere in the city was so dark, the people so vengeful and unpredictable, and innocent citizens were executed so often on mere suspicion and hatred, that she couldn't forget that many others just as innocent as her husband were executed every day. Her heart was still loaded with worry.
ko: 도시의 분위기는 너무나 어두웠고, 사람들은 매우 복수심에 불타고 예측할 수 없었으며, 무고한 시민들이 단지 의심과 증오만으로 자주 처형되었기 때문에, 그녀는 남편만큼이나 무고한 수많은 사람들이 매일 처형당하고 있다는 사실을 잊을 수 없었다. 그녀의 마음은 여전히 걱정으로 가득 차 있었다.

raw: The shadows of the wintry afternoon were beginning to fall, and even now the dreadful carts were rolling through the streets.
en: As the winter afternoon grew dark, she knew the terrible carts were rumbled through the streets.
ko: 겨울 오후가 어두워질 때, 그녀는 끔찍한 수레들이 거리를 덜컹거리며 지나가고 있다는 것을 알았다.

raw: Her mind pursued them, looking for him among the Condemned; and then she clung closer to his real presence and trembled more.
en: She imagined Charles in them, and she clung tighter to his arm and shivered even more.
ko: 그녀는 찰스가 그 수레 안에 있는 것을 상상했고, 그의 팔에 더 꼭 매달리며 더욱 몸을 떨었다.

raw: Her father, cheering her, showed a compassionate superiority to this woman’s weakness, which was wonderful to see.
en: Her father, cheered her up, showing a kind confidence that looked past her fears.
ko: 그녀의 아버지는 그녀의 두려움을 꿰뚫어 보는 다정한 자신감을 보여주며 그녀를 격려했다.

raw: No garret, no shoemaking, no One Hundred and Five, North Tower, now!
en: There was no shoemaking or memory of his old cell in the North Tower now!
ko: 이제 구두를 만들거나 북쪽 탑의 옛 감방에 대한 기억은 전혀 없었다!

raw: He had accomplished the task he had set himself, his promise was redeemed, he had saved Charles.
en: He had done what he promised: he had saved Charles.
ko: 그는 약속한 대로 해냈다: 그는 찰스를 구했다.

raw: Let them all lean upon him.
en: He wanted them all to rely on him.
ko: 그는 그들 모두가 자신에게 의지하기를 원했다.

raw: Their housekeeping was of a very frugal kind: not only because that was the safest way of life, involving the least offence to the people, but because they were not rich, and Charles, throughout his imprisonment, had had to pay heavily for his bad food, and for his guard, and towards the living of the poorer prisoners.
en: They lived very simply, not only because it was safer to avoid showing off, but because they were short on money. During his imprisonment, Charles had been forced to pay large amounts for his food, his guards, and to help support the poorer prisoners.
ko: 그들은 단지 과시를 피하는 것이 더 안전했기 때문만 아니라, 돈이 부족했기 때문에 매우 소박하게 살았다. 투옥되어 있는 동안 찰스는 자신의 식대와 교도관들에게 많은 돈을 지불해야 했고, 더 가난한 죄수들을 돕기 위해 강제로 비용을 부담해야 했다.

raw: Partly on this account, and partly to avoid a domestic spy, they kept no servant; the citizen and citizeness who acted as porters at the courtyard gate, rendered them occasional service; and Jerry (almost wholly transferred to them by Mr.
en: For this reason, and to avoid hiring a servant who might spy on them, they did their own housework. The gatekeepers of the building helped them occasionally, and Jerry Cruncher, lent to them by Mr.
ko: 이러한 이유로, 그리고 그들을 염탐할지도 모르는 하인을 고용하는 것을 피하기 위해 그들은 직접 집안일을 했다. 건물의 문지기들이 가끔 그들을 도왔고, 미스터

raw: Lorry) had become their daily retainer, and had his bed there every night.
en: Lorry, acted as their daily helper and slept in the apartment every night.
ko: 로리가 빌려준 제리 크런처가 그들의 일일 도우미 역할을 하며 매일 밤 그 아파트에서 잤다.

raw: It was an ordinance of the Republic One and Indivisible of Liberty, Equality, Fraternity, or Death, that on the door or doorpost of every house, the name of every inmate must be legibly inscribed in letters of a certain size, at a certain convenient height from the ground.
en: The revolutionary government required by law that the names of all residents be clearly painted on the doorpost of every house at a specific height.
ko: 혁명 정부는 법으로 모든 거주자의 이름을 모든 집의 문설주 특정 높이에 선명하게 칠하도록 요구했다.

raw: Mr.
en: Jerry Cruncher's name was already written on the doorpost downstairs.
ko: 제리 크런처의 이름은 이미 아래층 문설주에 적혀 있었다.

raw: Jerry Cruncher’s name, therefore, duly embellished the doorpost down below; and, as the afternoon shadows deepened, the owner of that name himself appeared, from overlooking a painter whom Doctor Manette had employed to add to the list the name of Charles Evrémonde, called Darnay.
en: As it grew dark, Jerry returned after watching a painter whom Doctor Manette had hired to add the name of Charles Evremonde, called Darnay, to the list.
ko: 날이 어두워지자 제리는 마네트 박사가 고용한 화가가 찰스 에브레몽드, 일명 다네이의 이름을 목록에 추가하는 것을 지켜본 후 돌아왔다.

raw: In the universal fear and distrust that darkened the time, all the usual harmless ways of life were changed.
en: Because of the fear and distrust during this time, everyday life was completely different.
ko: 이 시기에는 두려움과 불신 때문에 일상생활이 완전히 달랐다.

raw: In the Doctor’s little household, as in very many others, the articles of daily consumption that were wanted were purchased every evening, in small quantities and at various small shops.
en: Like many others, Doctor Manette's household bought their supplies every evening in small amounts from different shops.
ko: 다른 많은 사람들과 마찬가지로, 마네트 박사네 가족은 매일 저녁 여러 상점에서 조금씩 생필품을 샀다.

raw: To avoid attracting notice, and to give as little occasion as possible for talk and envy, was the general desire.
en: The general goal was to avoid attracting attention, and to give people as little reason as possible to gossip or feel jealous.
ko: 일반적인 목표는 관심을 끄는 것을 피하고 사람들에게 소문을 내거나 질투할 이유를 최대한 적게 주는 것이었다.

raw: For some months past, Miss Pross and Mr.
en: For several months, Miss Pross and Jerry Cruncher had been the shoppers, Miss Pross carrying the money and Jerry carrying the basket.
ko: 몇 달 동안 프로스 양과 제리 크런처가 쇼핑을 담당했는데, 프로스 양은 돈을 들고 제리는 바구니를 들었다.

raw: Cruncher had discharged the office of purveyors; the former carrying the money; the latter, the basket.
en: Every afternoon when the street lamps were lit, they went out to buy what they needed.
ko: 매일 오후 가로등이 켜지면 그들은 필요한 것을 사러 나갔다.

raw: Every afternoon at about the time when the public lamps were lighted, they fared forth on this duty, and made and brought home such purchases as were needful.
en: Although Miss Pross had lived with a French family for years, she refused to learn a single word of the language.
ko: 프로스 양은 수년 동안 프랑스인 가족과 함께 살았음에도 불구하고 단 한 마디의 프랑스어도 배우기를 거부했다.

raw: Although Miss Pross, through her long association with a French family, might have known as much of their language as of her own, if she had had a mind, she had no mind in that direction; consequently she knew no more of that “nonsense” (as she was pleased to call it) than Mr.
en: Even though Miss Pross had spent many years with a French family and could have easily learned their language as well as her own, she had absolutely no desire to do so. As a result, she knew no more of that 'nonsense' (as she liked to call it) than Mr.
ko: 프로스 양은 프랑스 가족과 여러 해를 보내면서 모국어만큼이나 쉽게 그들의 언어를 배울 수 있었지만, 그렇게 할 마음이 전혀 없었다. 결과적으로 그녀는 자신이 '헛소리'라고 부르기를 좋아했던 그 언어를 미스터

raw: Cruncher did.
en: Her way of shopping was to shout the English name of the item at the shopkeeper.
ko: 그녀의 쇼핑 방식은 가게 주인에게 물건의 영어 이름을 소리치는 것이었다.

raw: So her manner of marketing was to plump a noun-substantive at the head of a shopkeeper without any introduction in the nature of an article, and, if it happened not to be the name of the thing she wanted, to look round for that thing, lay hold of it, and hold on by it until the bargain was concluded.
en: Her style of shopping was simply to blurt out a noun right at the shopkeeper without any polite greeting. If it wasn't the right word for what she wanted, she would just look around for the item, grab it, and hold on tight to it until they reached a deal.
ko: 그녀의 쇼핑 스타일은 정중한 인사 없이 그저 가게 주인에게 명사를 불쑥 내뱉는 것이었다. 만약 그것이 그녀가 원하는 물건의 올바른 단어가 아니라면, 그녀는 그냥 그 물건을 찾아 둘러본 다음 덥석 집어 들고 합의에 이를 때까지 그것을 꽉 붙잡고 있었다.

raw: She always made a bargain for it, by holding up, as a statement of its just price, one finger less than the merchant held up, whatever his number might be.
en: She always bargained by holding up one less finger than the shopkeeper, no matter what price they asked.
ko: 그녀는 주인이 어떤 가격을 부르든 항상 주인보다 손가락을 하나 적게 펴서 흥정했다.

raw: “Now, Mr.
en: “Now, Mr.
ko: “자, 미스터

raw: Cruncher,” said Miss Pross, whose eyes were red with felicity; “if you are ready, I am.”
en: Cruncher,” said Miss Pross, her eyes red from crying tears of joy. “If you are ready, I am.”
ko: 크런처,” 기쁨의 눈물을 흘려 눈이 빨개진 프로스 양이 말했다. “당신이 준비되었다면, 나도 준비됐어요.”

raw: Jerry hoarsely professed himself at Miss Pross’s service.
en: Jerry hoarsely replied that he was ready.
ko: 제리는 목이 쉰 소리로 준비되었다고 대답했다.

raw: He had worn all his rust off long ago, but nothing would file his spiky head down.
en: He had lost his rusty attitude long ago, but his spiky hair was still as wild as ever.
ko: 그는 오래전에 무뚝뚝한 태도를 잃었지만, 그의 삐죽삐죽한 머리카락은 여전히 예전처럼 거칠었다.

raw: “There’s all manner of things wanted,” said Miss Pross, “and we shall have a precious time of it.
en: “We need all sorts of things,” said Miss Pross, “and it will be a task.
ko: “우리는 온갖 것들이 필요해요,” 프로스 양이 말했다. “그리고 이건 꽤 힘든 일이 될 거예요.

raw: We want wine, among the rest.
en: We need wine, too.
ko: 포도주도 필요해요.

raw: Nice toasts these Redheads will be drinking, wherever we buy it.”
en: I'm sure those Redheads in the streets will be drinking toasts with it.”
ko: 거리에 있는 저 붉은 머리 녀석들이 그걸로 건배를 하고 있을 게 뻔해요.”

raw: “It will be much the same to your knowledge, miss, I should think,”  retorted Jerry, “whether they drink your health or the Old Un’s.”
en: “It will be much the same to your knowledge, miss, I should think,” Jerry replied, “whether they drink to your health or to the Old One's.”
ko: “아가씨, 제 생각에는 그들이 아가씨의 건강을 위해 마시든 악마를 위해 마시든 별 차이가 없을 거라 생각합니다.” 제리가 대답했다.

raw: “Who’s he?” said Miss Pross.
en: “Who is he?” Miss Pross asked.
ko: “그게 누군데요?” 프로스 양이 물었다.

raw: Mr. Cruncher, with some diffidence, explained himself as meaning “Old Nick’s.”
en: Jerry sheepishly explained that he meant the Devil.
ko: 제리는 머쓱하게 악마를 뜻하는 것이라고 설명했다.

raw: “Ha!” said Miss Pross, “it doesn’t need an interpreter to explain the meaning of these creatures.
en: “Ha!” said Miss Pross. “We don't need anyone to explain these French rebels.
ko: “하!” 프로스 양이 말했다. “이 프랑스 반역자들에 대해 설명해 줄 사람은 필요 없어요.

raw: They have but one, and it’s Midnight Murder, and Mischief.”
en: They only care about murder and mischief.”
ko: 그들은 오직 살인과 장난에만 관심이 있으니까요.”

raw: “Hush, dear!
en: “Hush, dear!
ko: “쉿, 이런!

raw: Pray, pray, be cautious!” cried Lucie.
en: Please, please be careful!” Lucie cried.
ko: 제발, 제발 조심하세요!” 루시가 소리쳤다.

raw: “Yes, yes, yes, I’ll be cautious,” said Miss Pross; “but I may say among ourselves, that I do hope there will be no oniony and tobaccoey smotherings in the form of embracings all round, going on in the streets.
en: “Yes, yes, I'll be careful,” Miss Pross said. “But I hope those smelly men in the streets won't try to hug us.
ko: “알았어요, 알았어, 조심할게요,” 프로스 양이 말했다. “하지만 거리에 있는 저 냄새나는 남자들이 우리를 껴안으려 하지 않기를 바라요.

raw: Now, Ladybird, never you stir from that fire till I come back!
en: Now, Ladybird, don't move from the fire until I get back!
ko: 자, 레이디버드, 내가 돌아올 때까지 난로 곁에서 움직이지 마세요!

raw: Take care of the dear husband you have recovered, and don’t move your pretty head from his shoulder as you have it now, till you see me again!
en: Take care of the husband you just got back, and keep your head on his shoulder until you see me again!
ko: 방금 되찾은 남편을 잘 돌보고, 날 다시 볼 때까지 남편 어깨에 머리를 기대고 있어요!

raw: May I ask a question, Doctor Manette, before I go?”
en: Doctor Manette, may I ask a question before I leave?”
ko: 마네트 박사님, 제가 떠나기 전에 질문 하나 해도 될까요?”

raw: “I think you may take that liberty,” the Doctor answered, smiling.
en: “I think you may take that liberty,” the Doctor smiled.
ko: “그렇게 자유를 누리셔도 좋을 것 같소,” 박사가 미소 지으며 말했다.

raw: “For gracious sake, don’t talk about Liberty; we have quite enough of that,” said Miss Pross.
en: “For heaven's sake, don't talk about liberty! We have more than enough of that here,” said Miss Pross.
ko: “세상에, 자유에 대해서는 말도 꺼내지 마세요! 여기선 그것이 차고 넘치니까요,” 프로스 양이 말했다.

raw: “Hush, dear!
en: “Hush, dear!
ko: “쉿, 이런!

raw: Again?” Lucie remonstrated.
en: Again?” Lucie gently chided.
ko: 또요?” 루시가 부드럽게 꾸짖었다.

raw: “Well, my sweet,” said Miss Pross, nodding her head emphatically, “the short and the long of it is, that I am a subject of His Most Gracious Majesty King George the Third;” Miss Pross curtseyed at the name; “and as such, my maxim is, Confound their politics, Frustrate their knavish tricks, On him our hopes we fix, God save the King!”
en: “Well, my sweet,” Miss Pross said, nodding her head firmly, “the simple truth is that I am a subject of King George the Third.” She curtsied at the king's name. “And because of that, my motto is: Confound their politics, frustrate their tricks, and God save the King!”
ko: “글쎄, 내 사랑,” 프로스 양이 고개를 단호하게 끄덕이며 말했다. “간단한 진실은 내가 조지 3세 국왕 폐하의 신민이라는 거지.” 그녀는 왕의 이름이 나오자 절을 했다. “그래서 내 좌우명은 이거란다. 그들의 정치를 혼란스럽게 하고, 그들의 속임수를 좌절시키며, 신이여 국왕을 구하소서!”

raw: Mr. Cruncher, in an access of loyalty, growlingly repeated the words after Miss Pross, like somebody at church.
en: Jerry, feeling suddenly patriotic, repeated the words after Miss Pross like a response in church.
ko: 갑자기 애국심을 느낀 제리는 마치 교회에서 응답하는 것처럼 프로스 양의 말을 따라했다.

raw: “I am glad you have so much of the Englishman in you, though I wish you had never taken that cold in your voice,” said Miss Pross, approvingly. “But the question, Doctor Manette.
en: “I'm glad you are so patriotic, though I wish you didn't have that rough voice,” Miss Pross said. “But here is my question, Doctor Manette.
ko: “당신이 그렇게 애국적이라서 기뻐요, 비록 당신의 그 거친 목소리는 없었으면 좋겠지만요,” 프로스 양이 말했다. “하지만 여기 제 질문이 있어요, 마네트 박사님.

raw: Is there”--it was the good creature’s way to affect to make light of anything that was a great anxiety with them all, and to come at it in this chance manner--“is there any prospect yet, of our getting out of this place?”
en: Is there, ” she asked casually, which was her way of bringing up their biggest worry, “any chance of us leaving this place soon?”
ko: 혹시,” 그녀는 무심하게 물었는데, 이것이 그들의 가장 큰 걱정거리를 꺼내는 그녀의 방식이었다, “우리가 곧 이곳을 떠날 가능성이 있나요?”

raw: “I fear not yet.
en: “I'm afraid not yet.
ko: “유감스럽지만 아직은 아니오.

raw: It would be dangerous for Charles yet.”
en: It would still be too dangerous for Charles.”
ko: 찰스에게는 여전히 너무 위험할 거요.”

raw: “Heigh-ho-hum!” said Miss Pross, cheerfully repressing a sigh as she glanced at her darling’s golden hair in the light of the fire, “then we must have patience and wait: that’s all.
en: “Oh well!” Miss Pross said, hiding a sigh as she looked at Lucie's golden hair by the fire. “Then we must be patient and wait.
ko: “오, 이런!” 프로스 양은 난로 곁에 있는 루시의 금발을 바라보며 한숨을 숨기고 말했다. “그렇다면 우리는 참고 기다려야만 하겠군요.

raw: We must hold up our heads and fight low, as my brother Solomon used to say.
en: We must keep our heads high, as my brother Solomon used to say.
ko: 내 오빠 솔로몬이 늘 말했듯이, 우리는 고개를 빳빳이 들어야 해요.

raw: Now, Mr.
en: Let's go, Mr.
ko: 갑시다, 미스터

raw: Cruncher!--Don’t you move, Ladybird!”
en: Cruncher! Don't move, Ladybird!”
ko: 크런처! 움직이지 마세요, 레이디버드!”

raw: They went out, leaving Lucie, and her husband, her father, and the child, by a bright fire.
en: They went out, leaving Lucie, Charles, the Doctor, and the child by the warm fire.
ko: 그들은 루시, 찰스, 박사, 그리고 아이를 따뜻한 난로 곁에 남겨두고 밖으로 나갔다.

raw: Mr.
en: Mr.
ko: 미스터

raw: Lorry was expected back presently from the Banking House.
en: Lorry was expected to return soon from the bank.
ko: 로리는 은행에서 곧 돌아올 것으로 예상되었다.

raw: Miss Pross had lighted the lamp, but had put it aside in a corner, that they might enjoy the fire-light undisturbed.
en: Miss Pross had lit the lamp but placed it in the corner so they could enjoy the firelight.
ko: 프로스 양은 램프에 불을 켰지만, 그들이 난롯불을 즐길 수 있도록 램프를 구석에 두었다.

raw: Little Lucie sat by her grandfather with her hands clasped through his arm: and he, in a tone not rising much above a whisper, began to tell her a story of a great and powerful Fairy who had opened a prison-wall and let out a captive who had once done the Fairy a service.
en: Little Lucie sat next to her grandfather, holding his arm, while he whispered a story about a powerful fairy who broke open a prison wall to free a captive.
ko: 어린 루시는 할아버지 옆에 앉아 그의 팔을 잡고 있었고, 그는 감옥 벽을 부수고 포로를 풀어준 강력한 요정 이야기를 속삭여주었다.

raw: All was subdued and quiet, and Lucie was more at ease than she had been.
en: Everything was quiet and peaceful, and Lucie felt more relaxed than she had in months.
ko: 모든 것이 조용하고 평화로웠으며, 루시는 몇 달 만에 가장 편안한 기분을 느꼈다.

raw: “What is that?” she cried, all at once.
en: “What is that?” she suddenly cried out.
ko: “저게 무슨 소리죠?” 그녀가 갑자기 소리쳤다.

raw: “My dear!” said her father, stopping in his story, and laying his hand on hers, “command yourself.
en: “My dear!” her father said, stopping the story and placing his hand on hers. “Calm down.
ko: “얘야!” 그녀의 아버지가 이야기를 멈추고 그녀의 손 위에 자신의 손을 얹으며 말했다. “진정하렴.

raw: What a disordered state you are in!
en: You are so nervous!
ko: 넌 너무 불안해하고 있구나!

raw: The least thing--nothing--startles you! _You_, your father’s daughter!”
en: The smallest noise startles you! You are my daughter!”
ko: 아주 작은 소리에도 놀라는구나! 넌 내 딸이야!”

raw: “I thought, my father,” said Lucie, excusing herself, with a pale face and in a faltering voice, “that I heard strange feet upon the stairs.”
en: “I thought, Father,” Lucie said, looking pale and speaking in a shaking voice, “that I heard footsteps on the stairs.”
ko: “제 생각에는, 아버지,” 루시가 창백해진 얼굴로 떨리는 목소리로 말했다. “계단에서 발소리가 들린 것 같아요.”

raw: “My love, the staircase is as still as Death.”
en: “My love, the stairs are completely silent.”
ko: “내 사랑, 계단은 완전히 조용하단다.”

raw: As he said the word, a blow was struck upon the door.
en: Just as he said those words, a loud knock shook the door.
ko: 그가 그 말을 하는 바로 그 순간, 큰 노크 소리가 문을 흔들었다.

raw: “Oh father, father.
en: “Oh Father, Father!
ko: “오, 아버지, 아버지!

raw: What can this be!
en: What is it?
ko: 이게 무슨 일이죠?

raw: Hide Charles.
en: Hide Charles!
ko: 찰스를 숨겨주세요!

raw: Save him!”
en: Save him!”
ko: 그를 구해주세요!”

raw: “My child,” said the Doctor, rising, and laying his hand upon her shoulder, “I _have_ saved him.
en: “My child,” the Doctor said, standing up and placing his hand on her shoulder. “I _have_ saved him.
ko: “얘야,” 박사는 자리에서 일어나 그녀의 어깨에 손을 얹으며 말했다. “내가 그를 구했단다.

raw: What weakness is this, my dear!
en: Do not be weak, my dear.
ko: 약해지지 마라, 내 사랑.

raw: Let me go to the door.”
en: Let me answer the door.”
ko: 내가 문을 열어보마.”

raw: He took the lamp in his hand, crossed the two intervening outer rooms, and opened it.
en: He took the lamp, walked through the two outer rooms, and opened the door.
ko: 그는 램프를 들고 바깥 두 방을 지나 문을 열었다.

raw: A rude clattering of feet over the floor, and four rough men in red caps, armed with sabres and pistols, entered the room.
en: Heavy footsteps clattered across the floor as four rough men wearing red caps and armed with swords and pistols entered the room.
ko: 붉은 모자를 쓰고 칼과 권총으로 무장한 네 명의 거친 남자들이 방으로 들어서면서 무거운 발소리가 바닥을 쿵쾅거렸다.

raw: “The Citizen Evrémonde, called Darnay,” said the first.
en: “Citizen Evremonde, called Darnay,” said the leader.
ko: “시민 에브레몽드, 일명 다네이,” 우두머리가 말했다.

raw: “Who seeks him?” answered Darnay.
en: “Who wants him?” Darnay answered.
ko: “누가 그를 찾소?” 다네이가 대답했다.

raw: “I seek him.
en: “I want him.
ko: “내가 그를 원하오.

raw: We seek him.
en: We want him.
ko: 우리가 그를 원하오.

raw: I know you, Evrémonde; I saw you before the Tribunal to-day.
en: I know you, Evremonde; I saw you at the court today.
ko: 난 널 안다, 에브레몽드; 오늘 법정에서 널 보았지.

raw: You are again the prisoner of the Republic.”
en: You are a prisoner of the Republic once again.”
ko: 너는 다시 공화국의 죄수다.”

raw: The four surrounded him, where he stood with his wife and child clinging to him.
en: The four men surrounded Charles, who stood with his wife and child holding onto him.
ko: 네 명의 남자가 아내와 아이에게 매달린 채 서 있는 찰스를 에워쌌다.

raw: “Tell me how and why am I again a prisoner?”
en: “Tell me why I am a prisoner again.”
ko: “내가 왜 다시 죄수인지 말해주시오.”

raw: “It is enough that you return straight to the Conciergerie, and will know to-morrow.
en: “You only need to know that you are going back to the Conciergerie prison, and you will find out the reasons tomorrow.
ko: “네가 콩시에르주리 감옥으로 돌아간다는 것만 알면 된다. 내일 그 이유 정돈 알게 될 것이다.

raw: You are summoned for to-morrow.”
en: You are summoned for trial tomorrow.”
ko: 너는 내일 재판에 소환되었다.”

raw: Doctor Manette, whom this visitation had so turned into stone, that he stood with the lamp in his hand, as if he were a statue made to hold it, moved after these words were spoken, put the lamp down, and confronting the speaker, and taking him, not ungently, by the loose front of his red woollen shirt, said:
en: Doctor Manette was frozen in shock, standing with the lamp like a statue. Finally, he put the lamp down, confronted the leader, and grabbed the front of the man's red wool shirt, asking gently:
ko: 마네트 박사는 조각상처럼 램프를 들고 선 채 충격으로 얼어붙어 있었다. 마침내 그는 램프를 내려놓고 우두머리와 마주 선 후, 남자의 붉은 양모 셔츠 앞섶을 움켜쥐고 부드럽게 물었다:

raw: “You know him, you have said.
en: “You said you know him.
ko: “당신은 그를 안다고 했지.

raw: Do you know me?”
en: Do you know me?”
ko: 저를 아십니까?

raw: “Yes, I know you, Citizen Doctor.”
en: “Yes, I know you, Citizen Doctor.”
ko: 예, 압니다, 시민 의사 선생님.

raw: “We all know you, Citizen Doctor,” said the other three.
en: “We all know you, Citizen Doctor,” the other three added.
ko: "우리는 모두 선생님을 압니다, 시민 의사 선생님." 나머지 세 명도 덧붙였다.

raw: He looked abstractedly from one to another, and said, in a lower voice, after a pause:
en: He looked blankly from one man to another and asked in a quiet voice after a moment:
ko: 그는 잠시 멍하니 이 사람 저 사람을 쳐다보다가 조용한 목소리로 물었다.

raw: “Will you answer his question to me then?
en: “Will you answer his question for me then?
ko: 그러면 나를 위해 그의 질문에 대답해 주겠소?

raw: How does this happen?”
en: How did this happen?”
ko: 어떻게 된 일입니까?

raw: “Citizen Doctor,” said the first, reluctantly, “he has been denounced to the Section of Saint Antoine.
en: “Citizen Doctor,” the leader said reluctantly, “he has been accused in the Saint Antoine district.
ko: "시민 의사 선생님," 우두머리가 마지못해 말했다. "그는 생탕투안 구역에서 고발당했습니다.

raw: This citizen,” pointing out the second who had entered, “is from Saint Antoine.”
en: This citizen,” he pointed to the second man who had entered, “is from Saint Antoine.”
ko: 이 시민은," 그가 두 번째로 들어온 사람을 가리켰다. "생탕투안에서 왔습니다."

raw: The citizen here indicated nodded his head, and added:
en: The second man nodded his head and added:
ko: 두 번째 사내가 고개를 끄덕이며 덧붙였다.

raw: “He is accused by Saint Antoine.”
en: “He is accused by Saint Antoine.”
ko: 그는 생탕투안에 의해 고발되었습니다.

raw: “Of what?” asked the Doctor.
en: “Of what?” the Doctor asked.
ko: "무슨 죄로요?" 의사가 물었다.

raw: “Citizen Doctor,” said the first, with his former reluctance, “ask no more.
en: “Citizen Doctor,” the leader said with reluctance, “ask no more questions.
ko: "시민 의사 선생님," 우두머리가 마지못해 말했다. "더 이상은 묻지 마십시오.

raw: If the Republic demands sacrifices from you, without doubt you as a good patriot will be happy to make them.
en: If the Republic demands sacrifices from you, surely as a good patriot you will be happy to make them.
ko: 공화국이 당신에게 희생을 요구한다면, 분명 훌륭한 애국자로서 기꺼이 응하실 겁니다.

raw: The Republic goes before all.
en: The Republic comes before everything.
ko: 공화국이 그 무엇보다 우선입니다.

raw: The People is supreme.
en: The People are supreme.
ko: 인민이 최고입니다.

raw: Evrémonde, we are pressed.”
en: Evremonde, we must hurry.”
ko: 에브레몽드, 우린 서둘러야 하오.

raw: “One word,” the Doctor entreated. “Will you tell me who denounced him?”
en: “Just one word,” the Doctor begged. “Can you tell me who accused him?”
ko: "딱 한 마디만," 의사가 간청했다. "누가 그를 고발했는지 말해줄 수 있소?"

raw: “It is against rule,” answered the first; “but you can ask Him of Saint Antoine here.”
en: “It is against the rules,” the leader replied, “but you can ask the man from Saint Antoine here.”
ko: "규정 위반입니다만," 우두머리가 대답했다. "여기 생탕투안에서 온 이 사람에게 물어보시지요."

raw: The Doctor turned his eyes upon that man. Who moved uneasily on his feet, rubbed his beard a little, and at length said:
en: The Doctor looked at the second man, who shifted his weight, rubbed his beard, and finally spoke:
ko: 의사는 짝다리를 짚고 턱수염을 문지르다 마침내 입을 연 두 번째 사내를 바라보았다.

raw: “Well! Truly it is against rule.
en: “Well, it really is against the rules.
ko: 글쎄요, 그건 정말로 규정 위반입니다만.

raw: But he is denounced--and gravely--by the Citizen and Citizeness Defarge.
en: But he is accused, very seriously, by Citizen and Citizeness Defarge.
ko: 그는 드파르지 시민과 여성 시민 드파르지에게 아주 심각하게 고발당했습니다.

raw: And by one other.”
en: And by one other person.”
ko: 그리고 다른 한 사람에게도요.

raw: “What other?”
en: “Who else?”
ko: 다른 사람은 누구요?

raw: “Do _you_ ask, Citizen Doctor?”
en: “Do _you_ have to ask, Citizen Doctor?”
ko: 꼭 물어보셔야겠습니까, 시민 의사 선생님?

raw: “Yes.”
en: “Yes.”
ko: 그렇소.

raw: “Then,” said he of Saint Antoine, with a strange look, “you will be answered to-morrow.
en: “Then,” the man from Saint Antoine said with a strange look, “you will get your answer tomorrow.
ko: "그렇다면," 생탕투안에서 온 사내가 묘한 표정으로 말했다. "내일 대답을 듣게 될 것입니다.

raw: Now, I am dumb!”
en: I will say no more!”
ko: 더 이상은 말하지 않겠소!
